text:
alex_support: Heads-up: multiple hosted customers reporting 503/500 and timeouts starting ~10:05 UTC. Error rate spike on api-gateway (5xx ~14%). Some requests show auth failures + backend 503. Acme-prod and beta-01 called in.

erica_oncall: On it. Any recent deploys or model swaps?

alex_support: No user-facing deploys. Noticed a higher-than-normal stream of long-context requests and a couple of tool-calls. Attaching a small runner log snippet we pulled from the forwarded crash dump: 

```
[2026-03-18T10:06:12Z] infer-runner[pid:1423]: loading model: redwood/red-7b-quant-v2
[2026-03-18T10:06:45Z] infer-runner[pid:1423]: kv_prefetch: reserving 6.2GiB
[2026-03-18T10:07:01Z] infer-runner[pid:1423]: CUDA error: out of memory (alloc 512MB)
[2026-03-18T10:07:01Z] infer-runner[pid:1423]: terminated with signal SIGSEGV (Segmentation fault)
[2026-03-18T10:07:02Z] kubelet: container="infer-runner" exited (rc=139), restarting
```

alex_support: There's also repeated "kernel: GPU driver reset" messages on the node.

maria_infra: Confirming — nodes in hosted-eu-2 pool show GPU memory pressure and OOM kills across 3 pods. Autoscaler didn't add capacity fast enough because pod started with high mem request but actual consumption spiked due to prefetching/kvcache.

devon_engine: We shipped a quant profile tweak to red-7b-quant-v2 in the candidate channel yesterday that increased prefetch slice sizes for long-contexts. It was supposed to be conservative but could explain the jump. I did NOT push to production, but model rollouts can hit hosted via the model-catalog autodeploy policy for small variants — investigating.

erica_oncall: Mitigation plan (short):
- Immediately flip routing rule to divert high-QPS auth keys (account tier: enterprise-heavy) to fallback small-model pool (red-3b) for 15m.
- Disable kv-prefetch on hosted-eu-2 via config flag: runtime.kv_prefetch=false
- Scale up hosted-eu-2 GPU nodes by +2 (hot-add) and taint one node for heavy batches only.
- Pause any automated model-swap jobs for 30m.

alex_support: Notifying affected customers and offering temporary credits. CS (lee_cs) on thread.

deploy-bot: routing rule "fallback-heavy-auth" deployed by erica_oncall at 2026-03-18T10:12:30Z :white_check_mark:

maria_infra: Scaled hosted-eu-2 from 8->10 nodes. Runtime flag set on pool. We're seeing 5xx drop from 14% -> 4% in the last 2m.

devon_engine: I pulled runtime traces and confirmed a batching path where quant kernel allocates an additional GPU buffer per tool-call + kv prefetch; that combination exceeds peak for some long-streams and hits OOM. Reverting the candidate allocation tweak on catalog for production variants now.

erica_oncall: Customer impact summary: ~25 customers saw transient 503s, top two (acme-prod, beta-01) faced degraded throughput for ~8-12 minutes before fallback routing. Billing: token accounting still recorded calls; CS to evaluate credits.

lee_cs: Noted — reaching out to Acme and Beta-01 with incident note + offer for usage credit. Will collect any logs they can share for repro.

alex_support: Repro steps from internal QA (minimal):
1) Send parallel long-context streaming requests (context ~120k tokens aggregated across tool-calls) to red-7b-quant-v2 with kv_prefetch enabled.
2) Toggle tool-call with large action payloads (~300KB) to force extra buffers.
3) Watch for GPU mem climb -> OOM -> segfault -> 503 gateway error.

devon_engine: Followups / owner: devon_engine. Action items: add runtime guardrail to cap kv_prefetch reservation per-request, add OOM safety fallback to serve smaller-variant automatically on memory failure, and add an alert for GPU mem fragmentation >80%. Also add a canary rollout for any quant/kernel changes and a preflight test that simulates long-stream toolcalls.

erica_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. Monitoring for 1h, postmortem in #postmortems with timeline and root cause. If errors resurge, we will trigger emergency rollback.

alex_support: Thanks team — updating support tickets and CS emails now. :thumbsup:
